E. Inclusion of non-environmental factors in the discussion of environmental impacts.
The primary purpose of the National Environmental Policy
Act is to insure that the full range of present and future\nenvironmental effects of proposed Federal actions are taken into
account in agency decisionmaking. Although non-environmental
values are certainly relevant to the final "balancing" judgment
of the agency, the impact statement must give highest priority
to environmental values in order to serve the primary purpose of
the Act. This requires that the "detailed statement" of environmental effects required by NEPA must discuss environmental\nimpacts only. Non-environmental effects which are relevant to
national policy must be discussed in a separate section of the\nimpact statement.
The draft impact statement on off-road vehicles includes in the section "Environmental Impacts of the Proposed Action" a detailed discussion of several non-environmental effects. These effects should be discussed in a separate section of the statement. Including them with the environmental impacts only compromises the protection given to environmental values.
*
The Draft Statement's lack of initiative in identifying research needs is especially disappointing in light of the high hopes expressed by Interior's own ORRV Task Force report:
Government is answerable to the general public in keeping the outdoor recreation environment at its highest quality. Therefore, it shares the responsibility in studying the impact of the ORRV. The research conducted in the past, particularly on the long-range environmental impact has been generally incomplete and inconclusive. It cis essential, even mandatory, that additional studies be undertaken in an effort to secure answers to questions regarding environmental impact, safety, noise and related aspects of motorized recreation vehicle use. The Department of the Interior is prepared to take the initiative. (p. 69)
